# W2 Implementation Design: top-k Diversified Enumeration + Measured Ranking (Mirage/Heron-style)

> Status: **v1 design draft (2026-07-30). Design only, not implemented.**
> Landing: branch `hwu27/paper-joint-solver` (worktree `/projects/kzhou6/hwu27/triton-beta-3-paper-solver-wt`),
> package `third_party/tlx/tools/paper_joint_solver/`.
> Fidelity discipline: **not a single line of the paper-faithful 1:1 path changes**. All new functionality goes into the new subpackage `paper_joint_solver/enumerate/`,
> activated by CLI switches that default to off (`--enumerate-topk K`, etc.); without the switches, the behavior of `python -m paper_joint_solver`
> is byte-for-byte identical to the v6 final version (lineage isolation for the replication claim).
> Related: master plan `/projects/kzhou6/hwu27/jos-upgrade-plan.md` §W2; distillation interface hookup in `30-w3-ptxas-oracle-loop.md`
> and `10-w1-calibration-robust.md`; candidate source (b) connects to `50-cpp-surgical-patches.md` (no C++ changes needed, only consumes the existing dump).

## 1. Goals and Positioning

JOS's SMT stage is pure satisfiability: under the same (II, L, W) it returns an arbitrary satisfying solution, and solutions
that are equivalent inside the model rank differently on real hardware (§21 measurements: skew +70 TFLOPS; §18 bwd: the
2-group ping-pong gets dragged down by ptxas spills without the model knowing). W2 upgrades "return one solution" into
"enumerate a structurally diverse near-optimal frontier + adjudicate by B200 measurement", and quantifies the gap between
model ranking and machine ranking (Kendall τ). Within the upgrade plan, this is the workflow that **can, on its own, absorb
both classes of incidents: ptxas spills and multicast inversion**.

## 2. Enumerator Design (`enumerate/enumerator.py`, invoked incrementally from joint_smt.py)

### 2.1 Diversity key: label-independent samewarp partition signature

Diversity key = the partition of the operator set induced by `opw`, **not** the full `t[v,i]` assignment (the latter yields
an astronomical number of equivalent variants). joint_smt.py already has the `samewarp(u,v)` Boolean rewrite (the
implementation primitive of CROSS-WARPSPILLS); the signature is defined as:

```
sig(P) = frozenset( frozenset(op names within group) for group in P )       # canonicalized partition
```

For each unordered pair (u,v) in V, take the samewarp value from the solution, reconstruct P via union-find, then
canonicalize. The signature is invariant under warp-label permutation (the partition itself is label-independent).

### 2.2 Exact form of the blocking clause

The clause that blocks an already-seen partition P (one accumulated per produced signature, asserted into the incremental
context or merged in whenever the query is rebuilt):

```
Block(P) :=  ⋁_{(u,v)∈ same-group pairs in P} ¬samewarp(u,v)  ∨  ⋁_{(u,v)∈ cross-group pairs in P} samewarp(u,v)
```

Semantics: the next solution must split apart at least one same-group operator pair, or merge at least one cross-group
pair — i.e., produce a **different partition**. The clause contains only samewarp atoms (O(|V|²) Booleans) and never touches
the t variables, so all time-slot variants of the same partition are blocked in one
shot. The VL group is pinned by the VARIABLELATENCY hard constraint; its member pairs are excluded from the clause
(always-true/always-false terms removed).

### 2.3 Two-level signatures and enumeration order

- **Outer level (family)**: the structural predicate vector from `strategy_report.py` `(dedicated MMA group, dual-softmax separation, independent rescale,
  compute-group count)` (VL isolation is a hard constraint and not counted). The main enumeration loop advances by family: for each solution obtained, compute its predicate vector; if that family
  already has a representative solution, additionally assert a **family-level blocking** clause (the negation of the predicate vector, encoded as the negation of the corresponding combination of samewarp
  atoms — generated by the mapping function from `strategy_report` predicates to samewarp atoms), forcing the next solution
  to change family. This automates the manual workflow of the §17 FA4-exact probe and the §22 discriminating-probe sequence.
- **Inner level (partition)**: for a user-specified family of interest (CLI `--expand-family <predicate vector>`), drop the family-level
  blocking and use only the partition-level Block(P), enumerating ≤k_inner (default 3) representative partitions within that family.

### 2.4 Orthogonality with symmetry breaking + unit tests

The symmetry-breaking triple pins only the warp **label** order (w used ⇒ w−1 used). The samewarp relation is label-independent, so:
(a) symmetry breaking does not collapse genuinely different partitions — two different partitions must differ in the samewarp value of some pair (u,v), and breaking does not change
the satisfiable value set of samewarp; (b) label-permutation variants of the same partition are one and the same element at the signature level and are never produced twice.
**Pinned by unit tests** (`tests/test_enumerate.py`):
- `test_sig_label_invariance`: build a 6-node toy DDG, manually permute the opw labels of the same solution, assert sig is identical;
- `test_blocking_excludes_partition`: after asserting Block(P), re-solve, assert the new solution's sig ≠ sig(P);
- `test_symmetry_breaking_preserves_family_count`: enumerate to exhaustion with symmetry breaking on and off, assert the signature sets are equal
  (affordable on small graphs).

### 2.5 Near-optimal slack, k, and stopping conditions

- slack: fix II = I* (no concession on throughput); L ∈ [L*, L*+6] (FA4-exact needed +4 in measurement, leaving 2 of margin);
  W ≤ W_min+2 (bwd wide partitions need headroom). Enumerate each (L, W) grid point independently, with global signature deduplication.
- k = 10/case (CLI-adjustable). Stopping condition, one of three: (i) k reached; (ii) UNSAT within the slack window — **in this case emit
  the "near-optimal frontier complete" certificate line** (the family list is the complete set of structures under that slack); (iii) a single query timing out at 120 s is recorded as
  unknown, following the three-state adjudication discipline (unsat ≠ unknown); unknown (L,W) grid points are listed explicitly in the report.
- Operations: queries strictly serial; each query in its own process + `ulimit -v 150G`; attempts logged to disk one by one (reusing the v4/v6
  incremental-visibility and memory-gate infrastructure).

## 3. Dual Candidate-Source Architecture (`enumerate/sources.py`)

A single measurement harness consumes two candidate sources, unified into a **candidate description record**:

```json
{"cand_id": "…", "source": "jos-smt | modulo-topn",
 "case": "subtiled_fwd | bwd | fwd",
 "sig": ["…group member lists…"], "family": {"mma_dedicated": true, "...": "…"},
 "model_rank": 3, "model_cost": null_or_float,
 "solution": "path/to/solution.json",            // source=jos-smt
 "variant_id": 2, "schedule_graphs": "path.json", // source=modulo-topn
 "realize_path": "skc | emitter | cute | none"}
```

- **Source (a) jos-smt**: the solution.json families produced by the §2 enumerator; model_rank in lexicographic order of (L, W, production order).
- **Source (b) modulo-topn**: the `schedule_graphs.json` variants produced by the main repo's `TRITON_MODULO_DUMP_TOPN=N`
  (sorted by partition_cost, with variant_id); realization re-runs compilation with `TRITON_MODULO_SELECT_VARIANT=k`.
  `sources.py` only parses the dump and generates environment-variable combinations — **zero C++ changes**. Its sig is reconstructed
  directly from the dump's per-node warpGroup vector, isomorphic and comparable with source (a).
- Significance: the comment at `ModuloScheduleGraph.h:268-285` in the main repo states explicitly that the TOPN dump exists precisely so that "an external harness can check
  cost-model ranking vs measurement", and the beam-search design in `schedule_candidate_search.md` is plan-only;
  this harness is its fulfillment — one harness serving two engines, also enabling a lateral comparison of family coverage between "SMT frontier vs heuristic top-N"
  (written into the report).

## 4. Realization Path Protocol (`enumerate/realize.py`)

Priority and fallback chain (**iron rule: a ranking is valid only within a single realize_path** — emitter 215 vs skc 844 is a path
difference, not a schedule difference; cross-path numbers must never enter the same ranking table):

1. **SKC binding** (primary path): `skc/binder.py` derives ring depth/skew/register quotas from solution liveness,
   `roles.py` classifies by fingerprint. Binding succeeds → realize_path=skc.
2. **Out-of-family candidates**: when classify rejects (e.g., the bwd "MMA spread over 3 groups" R0 rejection), if that family appears ≥2 times on the frontier,
   extend `protocol_overrides` parameterization for it (an elastic item budgeted at 1–4 days); otherwise fall back to ③.
3. **emitter comparison**: `graph_writer` → `sched2tlx`, realize_path=emitter, marked low-confidence, compared only against
   same-path candidates.
4. **Unmeasured**: marked realize_path=none, counted in the coverage denominator, disclosed truthfully in the report (honesty discipline).

Phase B CuTe binding (skc_cute) is **used only for the champion's final measurement**: only FA4-isomorphic families can bind (quotas/ring depth/skew; grouping
topology cannot be bound), and it does not participate in inter-family ranking; the champion produces final numbers for all 4 shapes on the fa4_1cta skeleton.

## 5. Measurement Protocol (`enumerate/bench_driver.py`)

Pipeline: emit-check/binding dry run → (GPU) correctness gate (vs SDPA reference, fp16 tolerance; failing the gate means elimination, with the
reason recorded) → `do_bench(warmup=500, rep=500, quantiles=[0.5,0.2,0.8])` median.
- Main measurement @16384, single shape; the champion additionally covers 2048/4096/8192.
- Environment: exclusive whole-machine window on dgx003 (`8b200.sh`), steady-state warmup, accompanying `nvidia-smi` clock/power logging;
  compilation in parallel, measurement strictly serial; hangs handled via `killgpu.sh`.
- For each candidate, `ptxas -v` output (regs/spill stores/loads) is parsed alongside into the record — this is W3's oracle fact source.
- Budget: 5–10 min/candidate, ~3 h per case (k=10 + champion all shapes + re-measurement).
- **<2% difference discipline** (the §24.1 bimodal lesson): when the top two differ by <2%, run 3 rounds of re-measurement, record the distribution shape (bimodal flag),
  and report median + quantiles, never a single run.

## 6. Artifact Schema and Backfeed

`ranking.jsonl` (one line per candidate):

```json
{"cand_id": "…", "source": "…", "case": "…", "sig_hash": "sha256:…",
 "family": {...}, "II": 66, "L": 150, "W": 5,
 "model_rank": 3, "realize_path": "skc", "binding_hash": "…",
 "tflops_16k": {"p50": 844.2, "p20": …, "p80": …}, "rounds": 1,
 "ptxas": {"regs": 152, "spill_st": 0, "spill_ld": 0},
 "correctness": "pass", "status": "measured | unbindable | failed_gate | unknown"}
```

- **Kendall τ**: grouped by (case, realize_path), compute τ between model_rank and the ranking of
  tflops_16k.p50 over candidates with status=measured; this is the primary quantitative metric for the gap and goes into the final report.
- **Distillation registries** (two, JSONL under `distill/`):
  - `to_w3_spill_windows.jsonl`: `{sig_hash, ptxas.spill_st>0, spilling group id (SASS attribution or whole group),
    candidate liveness-peak window [t1,t2] (recomputed offline from the solution live grid)}` → the L0/L1 trigger input for W3;
  - `to_w1_coeff_candidates.jsonl`: `{structural predicate, systematic-slowdown evidence (constant x%±quantile gap within a family), suspected
    unpriced cost term}` → W1 calibration candidates (e.g., "rescale co-located with softmax is consistently slower" → TMEM read-blocking cost underestimated).

## 7. Experiment Design and Acceptance

- **fwd (subtiled)**: enumerate ~10 families in (II=66, L≤152, W≤6) (expected to include the v6 free solution, FA4-exact,
  rescale co-location, and MMA-dispersed variants). **Pre-registered prediction** (fixed in the doc, prior to measurement): the model treats them as II-equivalent;
  measurement will rank dedicated-issue structures above the free optimum (directional evidence from §21 skew +70).
- **bwd (the core selling point)**: enumerate under **the paper's nominal register budget (no --reg-budget)**, so that the 2-group
  ping-pong analogue and the 3-compute-group scheme both enter the frontier; measurement + ptxas parsing automatically rank the spill-free wide partition first —
  the answer the paper obtained by manually lowering the budget is delivered automatically by measurement, with zero manual intervention throughout; the logs are the evidence chain.
- **Acceptance**: (a) per case, ≥6 families reach status=measured via the SKC path; (b) the bwd ranking automatically selects the spill-free wide
  partition (and its TFLOPS ≥ the manually budget-lowered version); (c) ≥2 distillation rules are produced into the W1/W3 registries;
  (d) for each (case, path), output Kendall τ plus a frontier-completeness/coverage statement.

## 8. Module Layout, CLI, Tests, Effort Estimate, Risks

```
paper_joint_solver/enumerate/
  __init__.py  enumerator.py  sources.py  realize.py  bench_driver.py  report.py
tests/test_enumerate.py        # the three §2.4 unit tests + schema round-trip test
```

CLI (all off by default):
`python -m paper_joint_solver ddg.json --enumerate-topk 10 [--slack-l 6 --slack-w 2]
[--expand-family <json>] [--out-dir runs/enum_fwd/]`;
`python -m paper_joint_solver.enumerate.bench_driver candidates.jsonl --gpu 0 --out ranking.jsonl`;
`python -m paper_joint_solver.enumerate.sources --from-topn schedule_graphs.json`.

Effort estimate: enumerator + unit tests 2–3 days; sources/bench_driver 1 day (reusing run_ablations.sh and the existing
bench infrastructure); SKC out-of-family extension 1–4 days (the most elastic item); 2 exclusive measurement windows.

Risks and mitigations:
- Enumeration blow-up / yices clause store growing out of control → family-level blocking first, per-query timeout, process isolation (v6 lessons carried over directly);
- Many out-of-family candidates depressing coverage → prefer extending SKC parameterization over fixing the emitter; coverage reported truthfully;
- Cross-path incomparability precluding a global champion → state the ranking's jurisdiction explicitly; the champion is claimed only within the skc path + endorsed by the CuTe final measurement;
- Noise masking small differences → the §5 re-measurement discipline;
- Granularity mismatch between source (b)'s sig and source (a)'s (the main repo groups by cluster) → unify sig down to operator-level reconstruction,
  expanding cluster members before canonicalization.
